### Executive Summary
- Active exploitation is underway against **SonicWall SMA1000** (critical SSRF, **CVE-2026-102255**, CVSS 10); treat any internet-exposed SMA as potentially targeted today.
- **GitLab self-managed** has a **critical unauthenticated RCE** in CI/CD regex compiler (**CVE-2026-97229**, CVSS 10); prioritize patching/mitigation and hunt for suspicious CI/CD-triggered activity.
- Multiple **“drop-in” exploitation paths** emerged (WordPress Bricksforge RCE; Metabase SQLi PoC; Citrix NetScaler RCE patch); tighten external exposure monitoring and fast-track edge patching.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) SonicWall SMA1000 critical SSRF under active attack (CVE-2026-102255)**
- **What happened:** Reports indicate **in-the-wild exploitation** of a max-severity SSRF in **SMA1000** soon after fixes were released.
- **Why it matters operationally:** SMA devices are perimeter access points; SSRF-style bugs are commonly chained to credential theft, internal pivoting, and appliance compromise in financial-sector intrusions.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Confirm inventory/exposure of SMA1000; push emergency patch/mitigation or restrict management/access paths; review last 7 days SMA logs for anomalous requests and new admin/session artifacts.

**2) GitLab self-managed unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-97229)**
- **What happened:** GitLab disclosed an **integer overflow** in the CI/CD regular expression compiler enabling **unauthenticated code execution** on vulnerable self-managed instances.
- **Why it matters operationally:** Compromised GitLab can yield source code, CI secrets/tokens, runner abuse, and downstream supply-chain impact; attackers can quickly operationalize CVSS 10 RCEs.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Identify all self-managed GitLab and verify patched versions; monitor for unexpected GitLab service restarts/crashes and suspicious CI pipeline activity (new runners, abnormal jobs); consider temporary access restrictions to GitLab admin/CI endpoints until patched (assumption: feasible without business outage).

**3) WordPress Bricksforge plugin unauthenticated RCE exploited (CVE-2026-85097)**
- **What happened:** Bricksforge WordPress plugin has a **CVSS 10 unauthenticated PHP upload/exec RCE** with exploitation reported.
- **Why it matters operationally:** Common initial-access vector for web server takeover leading to credential harvesting, internal recon, and ransomware staging—especially if any marketing/vendor sites share identity or network trust.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Locate WordPress instances (including third-party hosted) using Bricksforge and patch/disable plugin immediately; increase monitoring for webshell patterns and new PHP files in upload/plugin dirs; block suspicious outbound from web servers (new beaconing) at proxy/firewall.

**4) “Edge / identity infrastructure” patch window: Citrix NetScaler critical RCE + Progress MarkLogic SAML auth issue**
- **What happened:** Citrix patched a **critical NetScaler RCE** (**CVE-2026-107406**, 9.5); Progress MarkLogic published a **SAML processing auth flaw** (**CVE-2026-85962**) (plus broader MarkLogic patching referenced).
- **Why it matters operationally:** NetScaler and SAML-enabled platforms are frequent beachheads; even without confirmed exploitation, these are high-leverage targets in financial environments.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Validate whether we run affected NetScaler/MarkLogic and prioritize patching if internet-facing; review IdP/SAML auth logs for anomalous assertion acceptance, unusual ACS/redirect patterns, and new privileged sessions.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **SonicWall SMA1000 (CVE-2026-102255):** Monitor **VPN/appliance HTTP request logs + firewall/WAF** for unusual URL paths/parameters and spikes from single sources; correlate with **new sessions/admin actions** (ATT&CK: **T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application**).
- **GitLab RCE / CI abuse:** From **GitLab audit logs, runner logs, and EDR on GitLab hosts**, hunt for abnormal pipeline creation, runner registration, unexpected child processes spawned by GitLab services (ATT&CK: **T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter**, **T1106 Native API**).
- **WordPress RCE/webshell follow-on:** On **web server EDR + file integrity monitoring + web logs**, alert on new/modified `.php` in uploads/plugins/themes, suspicious POSTs to admin-ajax or upload endpoints, and outbound connections from web tiers (ATT&CK: **T1505.003 Web Shell**).
- **NetScaler/edge appliance exploitation attempts:** From **ADC logs + perimeter firewall**, look for exploitation-like request bursts, unusual user agents, and configuration changes; ensure syslog forwarding is intact (ATT&CK: **T1190**).
- **SAML/IdP abuse (MarkLogic/SAP/ZITADEL-related themes):** From **IdP logs (Azure AD/ADFS/other) + app auth logs**, hunt for abnormal SAML assertions, mismatched issuers/audiences, repeated failures followed by success, and new admin role grants (ATT&CK: **T1556 Modify Authentication Process**).
- **Metabase SQLi PoC (CVE-2026-72898):** If Metabase exists internally, review **reverse proxy/WAF + application logs** for suspicious query parameters and error patterns; watch for DB connection anomalies (ATT&CK: **T1190**, **T1505 Server Software Component**).
- **Ransomware ecosystem note (“pre-compromised edge devices”):** Use **VPN/firewall + EDR** to flag logins from unusual geos/ASNs and post-auth tooling (PsExec/WMI/remote services), and validate MFA on all remote access (ATT&CK: **T1021 Remote Services**, **T1078 Valid Accounts**).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch governance:** Add SMA1000/GitLab/NetScaler/MarkLogic to “24–72 hour SLA” patch class; verify compensating controls for any exceptions (segmentation, allowlists, admin VPN).
- **External attack surface review:** Reconfirm which **admin panels (GitLab, WP, Metabase)** are internet-exposed; reduce exposure with IP allowlisting, SSO/MFA, and separate management planes.
- **WAF/library hygiene:** If using **OWASP Coraza WAF (CVE-2026-104774)**, plan upgrade and validate rules relying on `t:jsDecode` to reduce bypass risk.
- **Supply-chain/dev tooling:** Track newly reported **Hex/Rebar3/Gleam** supply-chain CVEs; ensure dev build agents run with least privilege and isolated workspaces to limit path traversal impact.
- **Certificate lifecycle planning:** Start planning for **Let’s Encrypt 64-day certificates** (not urgent today) to avoid future renewal outages; confirm automation and monitoring for issuance/renewal failures.
- **Mobile/device risk awareness:** Remind teams to avoid untrusted Android devices (report of pre-installed malware on low-cost phones); validate mobile access policies for corporate apps/MDM.
